research_statement.objective: Document best practices for 7-day response windows
research_statement.scope: Incident coordination for multi-product SaaS vendors
success_metrics: Reduce duplicate updates sent to enterprise customers

key_questions.question: How do high-performing teams structure day-0 to day-7 communications?
key_questions.answer: They pre-stage templates, run twice-daily control tower syncs, and keep shared FAQ + timeline docs updated.

key_questions.question: What slows incident approvals the most?
key_questions.answer: Legal review cycles and lack of pre-approved severities add 18-24 hour delays.

key_insights: Control tower rituals shorten approval loops and remove ambiguity across teams.
Joint comms + legal slack channels keep reviewers aligned on latest drafts.
Enterprise customers prefer timeline-focused updates to RCA-first docs.
surprising_findings: Teams that published the FAQ early reduced inbound tickets by 43%.
recommendations: Pre-stage FAQ templates with scenario placeholders.
Stand up incident control tower channel with two-a-day cadences.
Record approvals inside shared timeline doc.

evidence.summary: Control tower syncs twice per day shortened approval loops by 36%.
Publishing FAQ drafts within 36 hours cut inbound tickets nearly in half.
Pre-approved severities saved 18-24 hours of legal review time.
